  PROBLEM: The last run changed the guard on the ceiling else-branch to check only for an open stretch (`[ -n "$REVIEW_RUNNER_WAIT_SINCE" ] && [ -n "${REVIEW_RUNNER_WAIT_RUN_ID}" ]`) and dropped the `review_waiting_for_runner` check; after an empty runs lookup sets `RUN_ID="unknown"` (line 514), `review_phase_deadline_extension_allowed` refuses the extension at line 118 (`[[ "$ext_run_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1`), so Phase 4 prints `E2E_REVIEW_RUNNER_WAIT ... outcome=ceiling` and the "::error::... when the ceiling was reached ..." message, then exits status=timeout while NOW is still below REVIEW_PHASE_DEADLINE_CEILING.
  WHY: A single failed or empty runs read past the 90-minute base deadline ends Phase 4 up to about 3 hours before the ceiling, which defeats issue #9480's goal; the contractual `outcome=ceiling` line and the queue `::error::` misreport the cause, and this is a regression from the last run. No test covers it, because `_RW_STUB` always returns the run. All reviewers rated it MAJOR. Suggested minimal fix: in `review_phase_deadline_extension_allowed` before line 118, add `if [ -n "${REVIEW_RUNNER_WAIT_RUN_ID:-}" ] && ! [[ "$ext_run_id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then return 0; fi`, and optionally gate `outcome=ceiling` on `NOW + POLL_INTERVAL >= REVIEW_PHASE_DEADLINE_CEILING`.
